content_preview.title: Docker Says a Docker Hub Account-Conversion Flaw, CVE-2026-105445, Let Reassigned Personal Access Tokens Act as Other Users Until a September 30 Fix
content_preview.summary: Docker's advisory says account conversion reassigned personal access tokens to new owners from August 2024 until a September 30, 2026 fix; it reports no evidence of exploitation.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Docker disclosed on October 12 a flaw in Docker Hub's account-to-organization conversion feature, tracked as CVE-2026-105445, in which personal access tokens (PATs) of a converted account were reassigned to the person named as the new organization owner while the token secret stayed unchanged, according to [Docker's security advisory](https://www.docker.com/blog/docker-hub-security-advisory-cve-2026-105445/). Docker says it deployed a fix on September 30, 2026, and says it found no ...

recommendations: Allowlist gaps resolved by the Chief Editor: docker.com and cveawg.mitre.org added to config/source_allowlist.txt; ghostpat.com deliberately not added (see editor_notes.concerns). No corrections file is needed.

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear News structure (Overview, what Docker says happened, rating and identifiers, timeline, review findings, researchers' account, unknowns). Vendor claims are consistently attributed ('Docker says', 'according to the advisory'). Title is 148 characters, counted character by character (cap 150, no violation). Body is 958 words both raw and with link URLs stripped (News range 400-1200, compliant). The summary is supported and carries the 'no evidence of exploitation' qualifier. Freshness is handled: the article states the advisory is dated October 12, the reports October 13, and that the fix has not been independently tested. The title's 'Let Reassigned Personal Access Tokens Act as Other Users' is supported: Docker writes 'a re-assigned PAT acted as the target user at the registry level' and the CVE record says the PAT 'authenticated to the registry as the recipient'. The title is prefixed 'Docker Says' and does not claim confirmed exploitation. Docker's own wording is 'could potentially pull, push, and/or delete', and the body preserves that hedge. Minor observations: the body gives Docker's own four-step description of the attack sequence in one sentence (high level, no commands, no PoC, no endpoints, flaw is fixed and transferred tokens deactivated), which is acceptable; no internal links; no BleepingComputer content.
editor_notes.source_verification: Manifest checked: all four snapshots exist (status 200), non-empty, contain the real page body, and no entry has suspicious_patterns. source-0.html.gz (docker.com advisory, 240160 bytes): body extracted from <main>; confirmed Posted Oct 12, 2026, author Mark Lechner (page shows both 'CISO, Docker' and alt text 'Chief Security Officer at Docker'; the article says only that the page lists him as CISO, which is true and not misleading), conversion mechanism (PATs re-assigned to the named owner by changing the token's owner record, without rotating or revoking the secret; owner 'was not asked to confirm and was not notified'), 'a re-assigned PAT acted as the target user at the registry level... could potentially pull, push, and/or delete images', 'publishing images under a legitimate name... rated it critical', no web UI access and no password/email/2FA change, exposure window August 26, 2024 20:33 UTC to approximately [19:10] UTC on September 30, 2026 (square brackets as the article notes), 'Timeline (all times U.S. Eastern)' with 'EST' used in two sentences (October 2 5:30PM EST and October 8th 3:45 PM EST), all timeline times (11:40 AM report, ~1:30 PM reproduced, ~3:10 PM fix, 4:59 PM researchers informed, Oct 2 5:30 PM emails, Oct 8 3:45 PM deactivation with opt-out), fix 'less than four hours' after the report (3:10 PM Eastern equals 19:10 UTC, consistent with the bracketed time and the CVE record), ~304,000 pushes, 'We found no evidence that the vulnerability was exploited.', every push landed in the converted org's or new owner's repositories, static analysis of highest-risk public images found no malware or tampering, the quoted limit about registry logs, 'limited number of users', the Oct 2 email statement, remediation steps and user advice. The investigation section reports results for pushes only; pulls and deletions are not separately reported, as the article states. The advisory gives only 'critical': no numeric score, no vector and no CWE, as the article states. It does not mention Official Images. Reporter credit is Peter Molnar and Krisztian Hozak of mptrdev.com. source-1.html.gz (cveawg.mitre.org JSON, 2800 bytes, not a fallback): CVE-2026-105445, assigner Docker, published 2026-10-13T17:35:20Z, CVSS 4.0 baseScore 9.4 CRITICAL, vector CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H (PR:L, UI:N), CWE-266 Incorrect Privilege Assignment, affected Docker Hub from 2024-08-26T20:33:00Z to before 2026-09-30T19:10:00Z, reporters Peter Molnar and Krisztian Hozak of mptrdev.com, description says 'authenticated attacker' and 'pull, push, or delete'. All match the article verbatim; the article's statement that CVSS and CWE rest on the CVE record alone is correct. The CVE record's references list the Docker advisory as vendor-advisory and ghostpat.com as third-party-advisory. source-2.html.gz (The Hacker News, Swati Khandelwal, October 13, 2026; thehackernews.com is allowlisted): confirms the CVSS 4.0 9.4 score from the CVE record, 'Docker made the fix on Docker Hub itself, so there is no update to install', and 'The advisory reports results for pushes. It does not say what Docker found for pulls or deletions', which the article correctly attributes. source-3.html.gz (ghostpat.com, 23134 bytes, full page body, updated 2026-10-13): confirms two independent reproductions (2026-09-28 vector 1, 2026-09-29 vector 2), consenting test accounts ('No, our PoC used consenting test accounts'), login as the target, push to the target's namespace and to an org it belongs to, pull of the target's private repositories, zero notification in their tests, the recommended fix (confirm with the receiver and require explicit approval), and the section 'Worst case (flagged, not confirmed)' about Official Images. Live re-fetch: the CVE API record was fetched live and is byte-identical to the snapshot (same sha256 36b360f6...); the Docker advisory was re-fetched live (HTTP 200) and its extracted article body is identical to the snapshot (7209 characters, exact match). Neither changed. No page instruction aimed at an AI agent was found.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, date, name, CVE field and quote checked verbatim against the snapshots (details in source_verification). Quotes verified verbatim: 'was not asked to confirm and was not notified', 'a re-assigned PAT acted as the target user at the registry level', 'could potentially pull, push, and/or delete images', 'publishing images under a legitimate name', 'We found no evidence that the vulnerability was exploited.', 'registry logs show when a token is used, not that it exists, so a transferred token that was never used leaves no trace', 'limited number of users', 'Worst case (flagged, not confirmed)'. No field was dropped or generalised: CVSS version (4.0), score (9.4), vector, severity (Critical), CWE-266, affected window, reporters and the October 13 CVE publication date are all stated. Exploitation is reported as 'no evidence' per Docker, with Docker's own limit that an unused token leaves no trace. The article does not claim confirmed exploitation or confirmed affected accounts. Researcher claims (private repository pulls, no notification) are attributed to the researchers and contrasted with Docker's 'could potentially'. Official Images: stated as the researchers' unconfirmed speculation, with the note that Docker does not mention it. It is short, correctly labelled, and adds context on the researchers' view, so it is acceptable to keep; it is the one item I would have cut if space were tight. No fabricated specifics found.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; no sensationalism or editorialising; no AI self-reference. Vendor and researcher claims are attributed.
editor_notes.originality: No existing article covers CVE-2026-105445 or this Docker Hub flaw (searched src/content/articles for the CVE ID and 'docker hub' in 2026-09 and 2026-10). New story, published within two days of the advisory.
concerns: Allowlist: docker.com, cveawg.mitre.org and ghostpat.com were not in config/source_allowlist.txt, and matching is exact-domain, so the existing mitre.org entry does not cover the cveawg.mitre.org subdomain. Resolution (evaluated separately): (1) docker.com added, as Docker's own advisory channel and the authoritative first-party source for an incident on a service Docker operates, with the attribution caveat recorded in the allowlist comment. (2) cveawg.mitre.org added, as the CVE Program's own CVE Services API and the authoritative record of the CVE (CVSS and CWE come only from here); a separate entry was needed because matching is exact. (3) ghostpat.com NOT added: it is the personal write-up site of the reporting researchers (mptrdev.com), not a vetted publisher, and was not added merely to clear the warning. Citing it is acceptable because the article uses it only to report the researchers' own account, attributes every claim to them, labels their worst-case scenario as unconfirmed, contrasts their claims with Docker's wording, and both Docker's advisory and the CVE record link to it as the technical write-up. The script's allowlist warning for ghostpat.com therefore remains in the findings by design.

Verdict override: the script returned APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS solely because of the allowlist warning. After the manual review there is no article error to correct, so a corrections record would be inaccurate; the verdict is APPROVE with the reasoning recorded here.

No suspicious_patterns were flagged for any source, so no prompt-injection review was needed. BleepingComputer was excluded by the writer and the article does not draw on it (checked: no mention in the body or source list).

Minor: the body includes Docker's own high-level four-step description of the attack sequence in one sentence. It contains no commands, endpoints, proof-of-concept detail, and the flaw is fixed with transferred tokens deactivated, so it is acceptable.
recommendations: For future security articles, keep the researchers-only scenarios (such as the Official Images speculation) short or omit them unless the vendor addresses them.
When a vendor page lists a person's title two ways, say both or neither; saying 'the page lists him as CISO' is true but incomplete here (the page also gives Chief Security Officer).
editor_notes.overall_assessment: High-quality, carefully hedged News article on a high-stakes security story. All four sources were read from their snapshots and every claim, quote, CVE field, date and time-zone detail matches. Title 148 chars and 958 words are within policy. Allowlist gaps resolved (docker.com and cveawg.mitre.org added; ghostpat.com not added but acceptable as an attributed researcher account). No defects requiring correction. APPROVE.
